title: Repair: the triple loop
starter:
let matmul (a : int array) (b : int array) (rows : int) (mid : int) (cols : int) : int array =
  let c = Array.make (rows * cols) 0 in
  let total = ref 0 in
  for i = 0 to rows - 1 do
    for j = 0 to cols - 1 do
      for k = 0 to mid - 1 do
        total := !total + a.(i * mid + k) * b.(k * cols + j)
      done;
      c.(i * cols + j) <- !total
    done
  done;
  c
hints: Run the first sample. The first cell is right, and every later cell is too big. What is each later cell carrying that it should not?
Every cell of `c` is its own dot product, so its total has to start at 0. The starter sets the total to 0 only once, before all the loops.
Move `let total = ref 0 in` from above the `i` loop to just above the `k` loop, inside the `j` loop.

answer.code:
let matmul (a : int array) (b : int array) (rows : int) (mid : int) (cols : int) : int array =
  let c = Array.make (rows * cols) 0 in
  for i = 0 to rows - 1 do
    for j = 0 to cols - 1 do
      let total = ref 0 in
      for k = 0 to mid - 1 do
        total := !total + a.(i * mid + k) * b.(k * cols + j)
      done;
      c.(i * cols + j) <- !total
    done
  done;
  c
answer.explain: Each cell of the result is one dot product, so its running total must start at 0. The starter set the total to 0 once, so each cell also held the sum of every cell before it. The reference sets it to 0 inside the `j` loop, once per cell. Week 3 calls this the reset.
